youtube.title: A Signal From Space Lasted 72 Seconds. It Never Came Back. | The Wow! Signal
youtube.description:
On 15 August 1977, Ohio State University's Big Ear radio telescope recorded a narrowband signal lasting 72 seconds, close to the hydrogen line, from the direction of Sagittarius. Astronomer Jerry Ehman circled the code 6EQUJ5 on the printout and wrote "Wow!" in the margin. It has never been detected again. In 2024, researchers proposed a natural cause: a hydrogen cloud brightened by a magnetar flare. It remains unproven.

📂 Case File #023: The Wow! Signal

Sources: National Geographic, "This mysterious radio signal has puzzled astronomers for nearly 50 years"; History.com, "Wow! signal detected".
Images (Wikimedia Commons): Wow! signal printout, Big Ear Radio Observatory and NAAPO (public domain); Milky Way by ESO/S. Guisard (www.eso.org/~sguisard) (CC BY 4.0); radio telescope (not Big Ear) by Chimangolatino (CC BY-SA 4.0).
